https://chatgpt.com/?model=gpt-4&q=Summarize this helpful article from SEO and digital marketing leader WebFX:Title: "The History of CSS Resets"URL: https://www.webfx.com/blog/web-design/the-history-of-css-resets/Content:CSS resets are stylesheets that override each browser’s basic default styling to ensure more consistent display across different browsers. Early methods appeared around 2004, with two notable origins: Tantek Çelik’s “UndoHTML.css” and Andrew Krespanis’s “hard reset” using the universal selector (* { padding: 0; margin: 0; }). Çelik’s reset removed or standardized link underlines, heading sizes, and other styles. Krespanis’s approach zeroed out margins and padding for every element but could negatively affect forms and performance.Eric Meyer expanded on Çelik’s work, publishing his own resets that evolved over several revisions between 2004 and 2008. Meyer sought to “undo” each browser’s default styles while emphasizing that designers should customize these resets for specific projects instead of just dropping them in. Over time, key differences arose: some versions used the universal selector, while others selectively targeted elements to avoid performance issues and to maintain form styling. Another major reset approach came from Yahoo!’s YUI framework. Introduced in 2006 by Nate Koechley and Matt Sweeney, it zeroed out margins, padding, and other default browser styles on a wide range of elements, creating a “clean slate” that designers could build upon. Meyer’s own reset took YUI’s approach further by targeting more elements (such as applet, object, iframe) and removing features like outline, link borders, and default list bullets.Additional resets included Faruk Ate?’s “initial.css,” which avoided the universal selector from the start but received less publicity compared to Meyer’s or YUI’s. Many developers created custom resets tailored to their needs, often combining ideas from existing suggestions.Debate emerged over whether fully stripping all default styles is more efficient than selectively resetting only the elements actually used. Concerns include performance (due to the universal selector) and the extra work of re-styling everything afterward. Meyer and others argue that resets are a baseline—designers should refine each reset to suit their project’s requirements. Many developers still find them valuable for cross-browser consistency, while others feel they introduce unnecessary complexity.This article is Part 1 of a three-part series. Part 2 covers a comprehensive guide to different CSS resets, and Part 3 addresses whether web designers should use them at all.

https://chatgpt.com/?model=gpt-4&q=Summarize this helpful article from SEO and digital marketing leader WebFX:Title: "What Is Anchor Text? Your Complete Guide"URL: https://www.webfx.com/blog/web-design/anchor-text/Content:Anchor text is the visible, clickable text in a hyperlink. It often appears in a distinct color, making it easy for users to click and explore another page. It also helps search engines understand page context and relevance.Types of anchor text:1. Exact match: The anchor text matches the linked page’s targeted keyword exactly.2. Partial match: The anchor text is a variation of the targeted keyword on the linked page.3. Branded: The text includes a company or brand name.4. Naked link: The anchor text is the URL itself, such as www.example.com.5. Site name: A simplified version of the URL (example.com) without the “www.”6. Generic: Non-descriptive text like “Click here” or “Learn more.”7. Images: The image’s alt attribute functions as the anchor text.Anchor text SEO involves optimizing these links for better search engine indexing and user experience. Search engines use anchor text to understand page relevance and content. While you cannot control how external sites link to you, you can optimize anchor text within your own content.Best practices for anchor text SEO:• Keep anchor text consistent and concise to improve clarity and maintain a balanced look on the page.  • Ensure each hyperlink leads to a page relevant to the anchor text.  • Vary anchor text phrases and avoid overusing the same link repeatedly on the same page.  • Insert links naturally so they flow with your content.  • Limit the use of generic text like “Click here,” unless it serves a specific purpose (e.g., a clear call-to-action).  • Avoid using your target keywords as anchor text on multiple pages. It can confuse visitors and hurt SEO by indicating that more than one page is competing for the same keyword.By following these guidelines, you can create anchor text that supports both user understanding and SEO goals.

This metric reveals how people shop, which products they choose, and provides insights into marketing effectiveness.AOV is calculated by dividing total revenue by the number of orders. For example, $50,000 in revenue with 1000 orders results in a $50 AOV. A higher AOV means each customer is spending more on a purchase.To improve AOV, businesses can:  1. Cross-sell (offering related products to what a user already has in their cart),  2. Make product recommendations (suggesting similar or previously viewed items),  3. Upsell (encouraging customers to buy more of the same or slightly higher-priced items with deals like “buy one, get one half off”),  4. Offer volume discounts (“5 for $10” or “$4 each when you buy three”),  5. Provide coupons (“$10 off $50”),  6. Establish loyalty or rewards programs (incentivizing repeat purchases),  7. Set free shipping thresholds (encouraging users to spend more to avoid shipping costs).By analyzing AOV and applying these strategies, businesses can effectively increase sales revenue without relying solely on acquiring new customers.

The extreme back-and-forth causes the snow to melt rapidly while the ground stays frozen, not allowing the snow to fully sink into the soil.    Laroque said most of the snow ends up evaporating, causing "instant drought," similar to what the province experienced in spring 2024.  "Then the trees rehydrated, sucked up a lot of the ground moisture and then everything is just ready to be burned," he said.  He also noted Saskatchewan's forest and grasses were mainly brown from the dry weather and made great fuel for grass fires.  Lori Daniels, professor and researcher at the University of British Columbia's department of forest and conservation sciences, said the emergency wildfire situation in the province is the result of an emergency global climate situation.  "The further we are from the equator, we're seeing that those changes are amplified," Daniels said.  "In Northern Canada and the northern parts of our provinces and up into the territories … we're experiencing more than three times what the global average is in terms of temperature change."  Daniels said climate change is "the new reality" and it's unclear how long the province will be dealing with these fires.  "We need substantial rain to wet down our ecosystems, dampen these fires, and make our ecosystems more resistant to fire for the rest of the summer," she said.  "But there is a chance if we don't get the weather patterns that bring that rain, some of these fires may persist for a very long period of time." Lori Daniels is pictured in her back yard in North Vancouver on Monday, August 30, 2021. Lori Daniels, professor for UBC'S department of forest and conservation sciences. (Maggie MacPherson/CBC)  Not all is lost. Many ecosystems in Canada have adapted to large fires, Daniels said.   "They are tremendously resilient natural systems," she said.  "The seed banks that are sitting, you know, deep in the soil, the roots that kind of persist in the soil underneath, will re-sprout and begin to regrow even after fairly intense fires."  There are also many shifts in tree species that surround the areas of a fire. Daniels said trees like broadleaf, conifer and needleleaf tend to grow in quickly.   "Fire can also be a rejuvenating force," she said.  Daniels said some Indigenous communities have used fire as a part of their land stewardship.       The healing burn: How a Mi'kmaw practice helps protect the lands of Newfoundland      Indigenous communities in B.C. and California promote cultural burns for disaster mitigation      Indigenous stewardship holds the key to wildfire prevention in national parks, Jasper hearings told  "We are now learning in Western Canada from our Indigenous collaborators and Indigenous knowledge holders that there was tremendous value in using fire, 'low intensity fire' or 'good fire'," Daniels said.  In the spring and fall, a specific type of fire would be used by some Indigenous communities to burn off fuels that have accumulated over a couple of seasons to stimulate understory plants and to remove the density of trees.  "You're still maintaining a forest ecosystem around you, but you're changing the amount of fuel.""

In Step 2, open the scan in Photoshop, select the white background (using Ctrl/Cmd + Alt/Option + 2 for newer Photoshop versions) and delete it, leaving only the line art. Create a new layer filled with white underneath and lock it.Step 3 is about cleaning up stray marks on the ink layer with the Eraser Tool. In Step 4, “flatting” means blocking in placeholder colors. You use the Lasso Tool (with Anti-alias off) to select each area and fill it with distinct colors on a layer beneath the line art. This makes it easier to later select and modify specific regions.Step 5 focuses on coloring. Lock your flats layer, then use the Magic Wand Tool (Tolerance 0, Anti-alias off, Contiguous off) to select areas from the flats and fill them on a new layer. You can experiment with different color schemes, and because you have flats, any color can be changed at any stage.In Step 6, add rendering or shading. A simple approach is to add cel-shading by using one color for shadows. Select the areas to shade, create a shadow layer, and fill with your shading color. You can also add a new layer to apply gradients to selected portions of the image, such as the background.Step 7 introduces textures. You can use scanned watercolor textures (or brush packs) and drag them onto your main document. Use the flats layer with the Magic Wand Tool to delete areas of the texture you don’t want covered (for example, selecting the background or other regions). Experiment with Blend Modes (Overlay is common) and adjust Opacity for the desired look.Step 8 uses adjustment layers to refine the final illustration. Add a Solid Color Adjustment Layer clipped to the ink layer to shift the line art color. Lower the Opacity if it appears too strong.Finally, Step 9 is flattening and finishing. When you are satisfied, flatten the image (Layer > Flatten Image) and convert it to CMYK if printing (Image > Mode > CMYK Color).In summary, this tutorial covers scanning inks, isolating them, cleaning up, creating flats, choosing final colors, adding shading and textures, adjusting line colors, and then flattening for print or final output. These techniques enhance efficiency and flexibility in digital coloring.

https://chatgpt.com/?model=gpt-4&q=Summarize this helpful article from SEO and digital marketing leader WebFX:Title: "Information Architecture 101: Techniques and Best Practices"URL: https://www.webfx.com/blog/web-design/information-architecture-101-techniques-and-best-practices/Content:Information architecture (IA) is the practice of organizing and presenting content so users can find what they need quickly and follow a logical path. IA considers three factors: the user, the context, and the content. Applying IA to websites, blog posts, and even physical stores helps people locate information easily while staying engaged.IA has four main components: organization, labeling, navigation, and searching systems. Organization systems let you sort data into categories, whether by hierarchy, steps, or any other logical grouping. Labeling systems use concise names (like “About” for a tab) so users understand where to find material. Navigation systems allow visitors to move around a site (using methods like breadcrumb links and sub-navigation menus). Searching systems provide a tool for entering terms so users can retrieve information from various parts of a site.Dan Brown’s eight principles define solid IA:1. Object principle: Recognize each piece of content as unique and changing over time.  2. Choice principle: Limit the user’s options to prevent overload.  3. Disclosure principle: Present only what is needed for the user to proceed.  4. Exemplar principle: Offer examples to clarify complex material.  5. Front door principle: Account for multiple entry points into your site, not just the homepage.  6. Multiple classifications principle: Provide multiple ways to find information (like breadcrumbs and top navigation).  7. Focused navigation principle: Keep menus consistent across your site.  8. Growth principle: Design IA so it can scale as your site expands.To create IA for your website, start by researching how people currently interact with it. Group information into logical categories, such as products, services, and educational resources, and provide a search function for those who know exactly what they need. Use wireframes to visualize website structure before making changes. Finally, develop personas (representative users) to understand how best to meet audience needs.An agency like WebFX can help build an information architecture strategy tailored to your business. They have experience improving user experience, designing websites, and generating revenue through digital marketing. Requesting a free quote can be a good step toward optimizing your site’s organization and user satisfaction.

VGT carry forward is only applicable in the following two situations: Subscription Renewal Monthly Subscription Yearly Subscription Subscription Paused Subscription Renewal Monthly Subscription If you have a monthly plan set to auto-renew, any remaining VGT at the end of the month will carry forward to the next month. The carried over VGT will be added as additional VGT for the next cycle, while the VGT gained for the new subscription is referred to as Plan VGT. For example, if you purchased a Pro monthly plan on August 3rd and used 2 hours of VGT, your account will receive 4 hours of plan VGT when it auto-renews on September 3rd. The remaining 2 hours of VGT from August to September will also be added as additional VGT. The carried over VGT from the last billing cycle will only be carried forward to the following month. If carried over VGT from August is unused in September, it will not carry over to October. If a subscription is cancelled, the carried over VGT will be lost. However, if the subscription is paused, the carried over VGT will remain. Yearly Subscription The same principle applies to yearly subscriptions, where any unused VGT at the end of the subscription period is carried forward to the next annual subscription. For instance, suppose you purchased a Pro Yearly plan in August 2023 and utilized 24 hours of VGT out of the allotted 48 hours. When your plan automatically renews in August 2024, your account will receive 48 hours of plan VGT for the new cycle spanning from August 2024 to August 2025 and the unused 24 hours will be added as additional VGT. And, the remaining 24 hours of VGT from August 2023 to August 2024 will be added as additional VGT. The carried over VGT from the previous billing cycle will only be carried forward to the next year.
